free_tier.stated: Free open-source (GPL) self-hosted repository server; no quota because there is no vendor. 'Pulp is an open source project that makes it easy for developers to fetch, upload, organize and distribute Software Packages on-prem or in the cloud.'
free_tier.notes: Headline offer; binding constraint specified in limits.

per_object_cap.stated: No per-object cap documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
per_object_cap.notes: extraction found no per-object clause; some of these providers meter on object count rather than bytes, and some state no cap

retention.stated: No retention statement documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
retention.notes: extraction found no retention clause; the seed's limits text may still state one, see extras.limits_verbatim

egress.terms: Free by construction. Self-hosted; you pay (or don't) for your own bandwidth.

interface_detail: rest (pulpcore REST API), plus repository endpoints for rpm/deb/python/container/generic; also ships OCI images of itself
tooling: pulpcore REST API + `pulp-cli`, plus `podman`/`docker` for the container deploy and standard package clients against published repos. Documented at pulpproject.org/pulpcore/docs/. It is also the backend Fedora COPR uses, which is a working-scale endorsement.
chaining: Same self-hosted arithmetic: unlimited instances × your disk. Notably it is the engine under COPR's Pulp backend, so its per-repo retention setting (`retain_package_versions`) is the lever that makes 'unlimited' repos actually behave like storage.
limits_note: No vendor limits. Operationally: you must run Postgres + object storage + workers; 'unlimited' means 'as much disk as you attach'. No built-in public/anonymous CDN.
